title: introduce-mp-quant-threshold-benchmark-and-fragmentation-heatmap-reporter
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Add mp-quant-frag-bench: a mixed-precision quantization throughput benchmark with GPU memory fragmentation heatmap reporter. Useful for quantization policy tuning and capacity planning.
description:
Motivation: We lack a focused micro-benchmark that correlates mixed-precision quantization thresholds with sustained throughput and real GPU memory fragmentation under long-lived multi-tenant sequences. Teams tuning quantization profiles (FP16/INT8/quant-aware blocks) have seen throughput wins in short runs, but in production the allocator fragmentation and long tail of priming tokens degrades sustained throughput and increases OOM risk. This PR adds a reproducible test harness and a visual heatmap reporter to make that interaction measurable.

What this PR adds: mp-quant-frag-bench (new CLI + python runner) that: 1) runs configurable mixed-precision thresholds across model submodules; 2) emits an allocator-level fragmentation metric FFR (Free Fragmentation Ratio = largest_free_block / total_free); 3) simulates mixed tenant workloads by parameterized interleaving of short/long sequences and context-cuts; 4) produces machine-readable outputs (ndjson) and an HTML heatmap + SVG that maps sequence position vs FFR and throughput.

Key implementation notes: - Benchmark harness lives under bench/mp_quant_frag/ with runner.py, driver_config.yaml, and a lightweight C extension that samples CUDA allocator free lists (best-effort; falls back to NVTX-only on unsupported drivers). - Added a warmup strategy that mirrors production prefix priming so quantization warmup effects are captured. - Introduces a small estimator for quantization-induced kernel eviction pressure to correlate with fragmentation spikes. - Added a reporter that aggregates runs into a delta heatmap and a per-bucket p95/p99 throughput table consumed by the perf dashboard.

Checklist: - [x] Basic harness + CLI - [x] Unit tests for config parsing and reporter aggregation - [x] Perf run on dev cluster (A100-40GB) - [x] Heatmap generation and HTML artifact upload step - [x] Documentation snippet in bench/README.md

Commits (high-level): - feat: add mp_quant_frag runner and core sampling extension - test: add unit tests for config parsing and FFR calculation - perf: baseline run data for model-neo-3b and redwood-tiny-1b - docs: usage and dashboard wiring notes - ci: add perf workflow step and artifact retention 14 days

Files changed (high level): - bench/mp_quant_frag/runner.py (new) - bench/mp_quant_frag/sampler_c_ext.c (new) - bench/mp_quant_frag/reporter.py (new) - bench/mp_quant_frag/driver_config.yaml (new) - bench/mp_quant_frag/tests/test_config.py (new) - bench/README.md (updated) - .github/workflows/perf-bench.yml (updated to add artifact publish) - bench/data_examples/ (added sample ndjson outputs)

Small illustrative diff (reporter header): --- reporter.py +++ reporter.py @@ def compute_ffr(heap_snapshot): -    # placeholder implementation +    # compute largest contiguous free block and total free to form FFR +    largest = _find_largest_free_block(heap_snapshot) +    total_free = sum(region[1] for region in heap_snapshot if region[0] == 'free') +    return largest / max(1, total_free)

Two asks: (1) make FFR computation robust when total_free is very small and annotate when sampling is best-effort; (2) add a smoke test that runs the HTML reporter headlessly so we catch regressions." Priya Nair (author) 2024-10-16: "Addressed both: added guard for total_free and a headless reporter smoke test that validates SVG output. PTAL." Avery Collins (reviewer) 2024-10-18: "Can we add a short note in the perf dashboard wiring about how to interpret FFR vs throughput? I can add a blurb on the dashboard side after merge." Priya Nair (author) 2024-10-18: "Added bench/README.md section 'Interpreting FFR heatmaps' and wired the HTML artifact path in perf-bench.yml."

Follow-ups noted in PR: - ENG-2210: add allocator-simulator mode to produce deterministic fragmentation patterns for CI (drafted) - Create a Grafana panel mapping run metadata to the heatmap artifact in perf dashboards (Avery to follow up)

Merge: Squash-merged into main 2024-10-22 by Jordan Lee. Summary: Adds the mp-quant-frag benchmark and reporter, CI perf artifact publishing, and documentation. The new artifacts will be used by the Optimize team for quantization policy tuning and by infra for capacity planning.

Usage example: ./bench/mp_quant_frag/runner.py --config bench/mp_quant_frag/driver_config.yaml --model redwood-tiny-1b --quant-thresholds 0.3,0.5,0.7 --workers 8 --out run-2024-10-18.ndjson

Notes/risks: - Sampler C-extension reads allocator internals (best-effort). On some older drivers the metric will be approximate — the reporter annotates that case. - Not a breaking change to infra; no runtime wiring required for production yet.

If you'd like, I can follow-up with a short notebook that overlays token-level latency with FFR to help SRE triage high-risk priming sequences.
